detailed_findings.finding: The induction structure is sound, with all required parameter bounds for applying the induction hypothesis implicitly satisfied when 0 < r < n.
The recurrence for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients is correctly derived directly from the q-Pochhammer definition.
The degree argument correctly avoids cancellation by observing that the two summands have different degrees and the higher-degree summand is nonzero.

reason: The proof correctly establishes the lemma by induction on n. The base case and boundary cases r=0,n are handled explicitly. For 0<r<n, the derived recurrence G_{n,r}=G_{n-1,r}+q^{n-r}G_{n-1,r-1} is algebraically correct, and the induction hypothesis gives both summands as integer-coefficient polynomials. The degree computation is also correct: the second summand has degree r(n-r), the first has strictly smaller degree r(n-r)-r, so no leading-term cancellation can occur, yielding deg G_{n,r}=r(n-r) and nonzeroness. The proof matches the lemma sketch and does not rely on undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
